{{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|2008 Argentina | [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Mason Alexander Plumlee''' (born March 5, 1990), nicknamed "'''Plumdog Millionaire'''", is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He primarily plays the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. As a freshman in 2009–10, he was a back-up forward for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|national championship]] [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|team]], playing with his older brother [[Miles Plumlee|Miles]]. He was a 2009 [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] in high school.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4496541|title=Plumlee finding way on the court|access-date=April 5, 2010|date=September 23, 2009|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Lawlor, Christopher|archive-date=July 21, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130721155656/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncaa/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4496541|url-status=live}} During his senior year at Duke, he also played with his younger brother [[Marshall Plumlee|Marshall]]. He was selected with the 22nd overall pick by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the [[2013 NBA draft]]. Plumlee was also a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] that won a gold medal in the [[2014 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. ==High school career== Plumlee first attended [[Warsaw Community High School]] in [[Warsaw, Indiana]], before transferring to [[Christ School (North Carolina)|Christ School]] in [[Arden, North Carolina]], after his freshman year. At Christ School, Mason helped lead the team to three [[North Carolina High School Athletic Association]] state championships and a record of 99–8 over his last three years. He earned a silver medal with the 2008 USA U18 National Team at the [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]].{{cite web |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204812457 |title=Mason Plumlee Bio – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date=March 5, 1990 |access-date=April 3, 2010 |archive-date=January 30, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120130145908/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204812457 |url-status=live }} Plumlee was named a 2009 [[McDonald's All-American]] as a senior after he averaged 15.3 points, 10.1 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 2.5 blocks per game for the year, a Jordan Brand All-American, and a third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] and Slam All-American. He was named 2009 North Carolina Mr. Basketball by the ''[[Charlotte Observer]]'', and was twice an All-State pick. In addition, he competed in the [[high jump]] in [[track and field]], with an individual best jump of 6 feet 8 inches. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2008}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Mason Plumlee | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]]/[[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = Warsaw, Indiana | highschool = [[Christ School (North Carolina)|Christ School]] (NC) | feet = 6 | inches = 10.5 | weight = 207.5 | 40 = | commitdate = February 27, 2008 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 4 | espn grade = 98 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2009 | rivals ref title = Duke Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2009 Duke Basketball Commits | espn ref title = ESPN | rivals school = duke | scout s = 167 | espn schoolid = 150 | scout overall = 6 ([[Power forward (basketball)|PF]]) | rivals overall = 55, 14 (PF) | espn overall = 10, 2 ([[Center (basketball)|C]]) | accessdate = | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Mason Plumlee 2011 - FEB 13 - Miami Hurricanes at Duke Blue Devils.jpg|thumb|Plumlee going up for a dunk for Duke in 2011]] His brother Miles had originally committed to play at Stanford, but chose to follow him to Duke after Stanford coach [[Trent Johnson]] left for [[Louisiana State University|LSU]]. He missed the first six games of the 2009–10 season with a broken left wrist.{{cite news |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/acc/2009-11-12-duke-plumlee_N.htm |title=Duke's Mason Plumlee out indefinitely with broken wrist |work=USAToday.com |date=November 12, 2009 |access-date=July 3, 2013 |archive-date=October 26, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026111539/http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/acc/2009-11-12-duke-plumlee_N.htm |url-status=live }}{{cite web |url=http://www.newsobserver.com/2010/01/07/272691/mason-plumlee-a-key-for-duke.html |title=Mason Plumlee a key for Duke – Duke |publisher=NewsObserver.com |date=January 7, 2010 |access-date=April 3, 2010 |archive-date=March 26, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100326142727/http://www.newsobserver.com/2010/01/07/272691/mason-plumlee-a-key-for-duke.html |url-status=live }} He and Miles usually rotated into games together, replacing [[Brian Zoubek]] and [[Lance Thomas]], and were often the first two players off the bench.{{cite web |url=http://www2.journalnow.com/content/2010/apr/01/sticking-together/ |title=Sticking Together: Plumlee brothers finding their comfort level with Blue Devils |publisher=.journalnow.com |access-date=April 3, 2010 |archive-date=April 4, 2010 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20100404033523/http://www2.journalnow.com/content/2010/apr/01/sticking-together/ |url-status=live }} Teammate [[Nolan Smith]] said: "He's an athlete. He can run and jump with the best of them in the country."{{cite web |url=http://www.heraldsun.com/view/full_story/4961988/article-Mason-Plumlee-returns-to-full-workouts-with-Blue-Devils |title=Mason Plumlee returns to full workouts with Blue Devils |publisher=The Herald-Sun |access-date=April 5, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100217075029/http://www.heraldsun.com/view/full_story/4961988/article-Mason-Plumlee-returns-to-full-workouts-with-Blue-Devils |archive-date=February 17, 2010 |url-status=dead}} Through April 4, 2010, Mason was tied for first on the team in blocks, with 30, and second on the team with 21 dunks.{{cite web |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204922369 |title=Game Notes: vs. Butler, April 5, 9:21 PM, CBS – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |access-date=April 5, 2010 |archive-date=May 26, 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240526153339/https://www.webcitation.org/6GngxtCRZ?url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml%3FSPSID=22724 |url-status=live }} In an average 14.1 minutes of play per game during the 2009–10 season, he averaged 3.1 rebounds and .9 blocks.{{cite web |url=http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/statlines.php?playerid=2740 |title=The Official On-Line Home Of Duke Statistics |publisher=GoDuke.StatsGeek.com |access-date=April 3, 2010 |archive-date=April 5, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100405015726/http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/statlines.php?playerid=2740 |url-status=live }} Coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] said: "Mason has got a chance to be really, really good. He has skills of a guard and the body of a big man, and a great basketball mind. He's very competitive, he likes the stage, and he's comfortable with the ball."{{cite web |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204822517 |title=Plumlees Relish Chance to Play Together – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |access-date=April 5, 2010 |archive-date=March 7, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120307165207/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204822517 |url-status=live }} It was anticipated that in 2010–11 the two brothers would both be in Duke's starting lineup.{{cite web |url=http://www.newsobserver.com/2010/04/02/418963/dukes-kelly-enjoying-the-moment.html |title=Duke's Kelly enjoying the moment – Duke |publisher=NewsObserver.com |access-date=April 3, 2010 |archive-date=June 5, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605084302/http://www.newsobserver.com/2010/04/02/418963/dukes-kelly-enjoying-the-moment.html |url-status=live }} [[Georgia Tech]] coach [[Paul Hewitt]] viewed Mason as Duke's best pro prospect.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/tournament/2010/columns/story?columnist=katz_andy&id=5045989 |title=2010 NCAA tournament: A coaching view of the Final Four – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=January 1, 2008 |access-date=April 3, 2010 |archive-date=April 4, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100404125057/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/tournament/2010/columns/story?columnist=katz_andy&id=5045989 |url-status=live }} Told in early April 2010 that some scouting services viewed him as the team's best pro prospect, Plumlee said: "I have seen that. I don't even really know what to say to those people. I mean, let's be real. I'm trying to play the best I can, but in reality nobody goes from the bench to the NBA. Come on."{{cite web |url=http://www.news-record.com/content/2010/04/01/article/dukes_smith_always_mindful_of_his_dad |title=Duke's Smith always mindful of his dad : News-Record.com : Greensboro & the Triad's most trusted source for local news and analysis |publisher=News-Record.com |access-date=April 3, 2010 |archive-date=September 6, 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120906005706/http://www.news-record.com/content/2010/04/01/article/dukes_smith_always_mindful_of_his_dad |url-status=live }} Mason started 11 of the team's first 13 games in the 2010–2011 season, in 3 of which he recorded double doubles in points and rebounds. For the season, he averaged 7.5 points, 8 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks per game to help man the paint for the defending champion Blue Devils. He was a 2012–13 first team [[Academic All-American]] selection.{{cite web|url=http://www.cosida.com/news.aspx?id=3973|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130408011013/http://www.cosida.com/news.aspx?id=3973|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 8, 2013|title=Delaware's Elena Delle Donne, Ohio State's Aaron Craft top Capital One Academic All-America® Division I Basketball Teams|access-date=February 21, 2013|date=February 21, 2013|publisher=[[College Sports Information Directors of America]]}} He was also a 2012–13 [[List of Senior CLASS Award men's basketball winners|Senior CLASS Award]] finalist.{{cite web|url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020613aad.html|title=Hulls Named Finalist for Senior CLASS Award|access-date=February 13, 2013|date=February 6, 2013|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=IUHoosiers.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130215113340/http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020613aad.html|archive-date=February 15, 2013}} ==Professional career== ===Brooklyn Nets (2013–2015)=== ====2013–14 season==== Plumlee was selected with the 22nd overall pick by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the [[2013 NBA draft]]. On July 3, 2013, he signed his rookie-scale contract with the Nets.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-sign-2013-first-round-pick-mason-plumlee|title=Nets Sign 2013 First Round Pick Mason Plumlee|work=The Official Site of the Brooklyn Nets|access-date=March 13, 2015|archive-date=September 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140924042336/http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-sign-2013-first-round-pick-mason-plumlee|url-status=live}} On November 15, 2013, in his first game against his brother Miles and the [[Phoenix Suns]], he recorded 7 points, 3 rebounds and 2 assists in a 100–98 overtime win.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131115/BKNPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Nets at Suns|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 13, 2015|archive-date=April 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402003418/http://www.nba.com/games/20131115/BKNPHX/gameinfo.html|url-status=live}} The following night, Plumlee played 26 minutes against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with both [[Brook Lopez]] and [[Kevin Garnett]] out injured, and had 19 points and 6 rebounds, both career highs.{{cite web|title=Plumlee goes Lob City on Lob City|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/brooklyn-nets/post/_/id/13689/plumlee-goes-lob-city-on-lob-city|publisher=ESPN|date=November 17, 2013|access-date=November 17, 2013|archive-date=November 18, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131118043827/http://espn.go.com/blog/new-york/brooklyn-nets/post/_/id/13689/plumlee-goes-lob-city-on-lob-city|url-status=live}} Plumlee was selected to play in the 2014 [[BBVA Rising Stars Challenge]] on [[Chris Webber]]'s team, while his brother Miles was picked to play on [[Grant Hill]]'s team. On February 9, 2014, Plumlee recorded his second NBA double-double, finishing with 22 points and 13 rebounds in a Nets victory.{{cite web|last=Robbins|first=Lenn|title=Nets Beat Pelicans; Lopez Confident About Returning Next Season|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/blog/nets-beat-pelicans-lopez-confident-about-his-return-next-season|work=NBA.com|publisher=NBA|access-date=March 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140924042444/http://www.nba.com/nets/blog/nets-beat-pelicans-lopez-confident-about-his-return-next-season|archive-date=September 24, 2014|url-status=dead}} On March 17, 2014, both Miles and Mason Plumlee started for the Suns and the Nets, respectively. Mason had 14 points and 11 rebounds, while Miles had 3 points and 6 rebounds in a 108-95 Nets win.{{cite web|title=Williams scores 28 as Nets beat Suns|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/williams-scores-28-nets-beat-025925554--nba.html|work=sports.yahoo.com|publisher=Yahoo|access-date=March 20, 2014|archive-date=March 22, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140322000913/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/williams-scores-28-nets-beat-025925554--nba.html|url-status=live}} On April 8, 2014, the Nets faced the two-time defending champion [[Miami Heat]], looking to become the first team to sweep [[LeBron James]] in a four-game season series.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2022774-brooklyn-nets-first-team-ever-to-sweep-lebron-james-in-regular-season|title=Brooklyn Nets 1st Team Ever to Sweep LeBron James in Regular Season|author=Zach Buckley|work=Bleacher Report|access-date=March 13, 2015|archive-date=September 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140924044733/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2022774-brooklyn-nets-first-team-ever-to-sweep-lebron-james-in-regular-season|url-status=live}} With Kevin Garnett resting his back and [[Andray Blatche]] out with illness, Plumlee was the only active center on the Nets roster. The Nets held an 88–87 lead in the closing seconds when James attempted a dunk that would have won the game for the Heat. Plumlee blocked the shot and secured the season sweep in what the ''New York Times'' described as a signature moment in his career.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/04/10/sports/basketball/blocking-lebron-james-cements-mason-plumlees-status.html?_r=0|title=Already, Nets Rookie Has Signature Moment|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=April 9, 2014|access-date=April 9, 2014|archive-date=March 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220320194502/https://www.nytimes.com/2014/04/10/sports/basketball/blocking-lebron-james-cements-mason-plumlees-status.html?_r=0|url-status=live}} Although James was visibly upset about the play, and claimed that he had been fouled, the NBA later announced that the call was correct and that the block was clean.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2025198-nba-rules-mason-plumlee-did-not-foul-lebron-james-on-crunch-time-dunk-attempt|title=NBA Rules Mason Plumlee Did Not Foul LeBron James on Crunch-Time Dunk Attempt|author=Joe Flynn|work=Bleacher Report|access-date=March 13, 2015|archive-date=March 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305014122/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2025198-nba-rules-mason-plumlee-did-not-foul-lebron-james-on-crunch-time-dunk-attempt|url-status=live}} In 70 games (22 starts), he averaged 7.4 points and 4.4 rebounds per game as he earned NBA All-Rookie first team honors, becoming the first Net since [[Brook Lopez]] (2008–09) to earn such honors.{{cite web|title=Mason Plumlee Named to NBA All-Rookie First Team|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/mason-plumlee-named-nba-all-rookie-first-team|work=NBA.com|date=May 22, Nets.jpg|thumb|Plumlee with the Nets in 2014]] Following the departure of [[Andray Blatche]], Plumlee came into the season as the primary back-up to Brook Lopez. On October 24, 2014, the Nets exercised their third-year team option on Plumlee's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2015–16 season.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Exercise Options on Plumlee and Karasev|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-exercise-options-plumlee-and-karasev|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2014|access-date=December 13, starting the first two games of the season in the absence of Lopez, Plumlee moved back to a bench role in the wake of Lopez's return until the starting center once again missed time during December, in which Plumlee was put back into the starting line-up.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/plumlma01/gamelog/2015/|title=Mason Plumlee 2014-15 Game added 10 rebounds on December 12 in helping the Nets defeat the Philadelphia 76ers, 88–70.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141212/PHIBKN/gameinfo.html|title=76ers at Nets|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 13, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150214043303/http://www.nba.com/games/20141212/PHIBKN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 14, web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141223/DENBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Nuggets at Nets|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 13, 2015|archive-date=February 18, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150218050842/http://www.nba.com/games/20141223/DENBKN/gameinfo.html|url-status=live}} On January 12, 2015, he surpassed his season high again with a career-high 24 points in a 113–99 loss to the Houston Rockets.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150112/HOUBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Rockets at Nets|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 13, 2015|archive-date=March 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150302080113/http://www.nba.com/games/20150112/HOUBKN/gameinfo.html|url-status=live}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2015–2017)=== Los Angeles Clippers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160106/LACPOR/gameinfo.html|title=Paul leads Clippers to 109-98 win over Trail Blazers|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive,
